amino acid infusions in the post-trauma phase in acute renal failure, in addition to the infusion of energy and fat, are of importance for the maintenance of the nitrogen balance and the improvement of the amino acid status in serum.
the administration of a mixture of amino acids in acute, compensated post-traumatic renal failure leads to improved amino acid serum levels in comparison to a single amino acid solution.
the amino acids of the 3 groups were well tolerated.

the question of how the different amino acid mixtures used for parenteral nutrition influence the serum amino acids in patients with compensated acute renal failure.

the question of whether the amino acid infusion therapy with a high glycine content (group I) or with a low glycine content (groups II and III) is more advantageous in the therapy of acute, compensated renal failures in the post-trauma phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid infusion of the 2nd patient group (250 ml EAS + 250 ml Intrafusine) is superior to that of the 1st patient group (500 ml EAS) with regard to the aminogram.
the 3 amino acid mixtures used in the present investigation were equally well suited in the treatment of acute renal failure in the surgical patient.

the amino acid infusion of 250 ml Eas pfrimmer and of 250 ml Intrafusine (group II) was superior to the amino acid infusions of 500 ml Eas prrimmer (group I) and of 250 Eas pfrimme and 350 Aminofusine Hepar (group III).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of amino acid infusions with different mixtures of amino acid is possible without any complications.
a combination of amino acids, as in group II, seems to be more effective than the administration of a single mixture of amino acids, especially for patients with acute, compensated renal failures.

a combination of amino acid mixtures of various composition and of different amino acids in the infusion solution, which is administered isocaloric and practically isonuritrogen, does not lead to any significant differences in the clinical course.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amino acid administration is a useful therapeutic tool in the post-trauma phase.

the administration of amino acid solutions in acute, compensated, renal failure is possible and can be performed with a variety of amino acid solutions, but that the amino acid infusion must be isocaloric and isonitrogenous.
the administration of amino acids in acute renal failure should be based upon a low protein diet, but with a high content of branched-chain amino acids.
